label: Personality
value: Agatha Sowerby is a pious Christian woman.
unit: A pious Christian woman who is deeply devout and actively involved in religious matters, she is known for her cheerful, gentle, and motherly nature. She is exceptionally kind-hearted and industrious, showing remarkable compassion and endurance as a caregiver while remaining an avid dressmaker. At the same time, she is an opinionated, candid, and often meddlesome talker who takes great pride in voicing her firm beliefs without partiality. Her severe, strict, and domineering tendencies lead her to actively train those around her and criticize others, including young housekeepers and college graduates. Although observant and possessed of great foresight, she can be pessimistic, lacking in delicacy, and burdened with a sense of responsibility for every concern of church and state. Her strong convictions also make her a passionate partisan who holds a bias against Yankees and firmly opposes higher education for women.

After the Liberals eventually secured an election victory, Ambrose shaved his long-kept beard, rendering him temporarily unrecognizable to Nell. Shortly after his transformation, Winifred announced her upcoming marriage to him.

label: History
value: Aunt Euphemia grew up in a family with around six girls.
unit: Aunt Euphemia grew up in a family with around six girls and was named Jamesina after her father, who tragically drowned at sea a month prior to her birth. In her youth, she routinely mocked and rejected her suitors, once advising a former suitor to wear an elastic strip to flatten his ears. She was forbidden by both her mother and her husband from owning a yellow silk dress, and she eventually received a cat named Sarah-cat as a gift from her laundress. Prior to permitting her daughter to attend university for mathematics, Aunt Euphemia personally taught her how to cook, and she later braved a personal fear of snakes to travel to India to investigate her daughter's mission field. In her later years, she moved into Tabby's Place with her two cats, Sarah-cat and Joseph, reassuring the young women living there that she would not enforce strict supervision over them. During her time at Tabby's Place, she offered guidance to Nell Harcourt on turning twenty and character growth, and she shared lighthearted conversations about her past romances with her young housemates.

value: Belinda worked as a young helper

While picking strawberries, she expressed her concern to Nell regarding Rosalind's declining health and melancholic mood. She was later delighted when Stephen Stanhope arrived and embraced Rosalind in the garden as a lover. Belinda was eventually reunited with Nell during a summer in Brierley and later attended Nell and Hugh's wedding at Grey Shutters.

label: History
value: Hugh spent three years in Alberta.
unit: During his youth, Hugh spent three years in Alberta with his ill father, during which he scarcely attended school. In his past, he also survived a severe fever, recited poetry during a school performance, and rescued Nell from a pond. Nell was also once forced to sit next to Hugh as a disciplinary measure during their school days. On the eve of their wedding, Hugh met with Nell before they moved into their new house near Seven Gulls Harbor, riding together in a buggy to their home where they were welcomed over supper by Doctor Dave, Mrs. Doctor Dave, and Captain Saul. Settling into their new life, Hugh shared his pride with Nell over saving a patient's life overnight and eavesdropped from an adjoining room while Miss Winifred Tolley visited. He later accompanied Nell on walks to the Seven Gulls light to visit Captain Saul, and listened as Nell shared her impressions of their neighbor Lorna Vane. Over the winter, Hugh hosted a successful first Christmas dinner with Nell for their friends, carefully carving the geese under Nell's instructions despite having baited Miss Winifred alongside Captain Saul beforehand. On New Year's Eve, Hugh, Nell, and Lorna walked to the lighthouse, catching a rare glimpse of Venus's shadow on their way to celebrate with Captain Saul and Ambrose Kerr. Across the seasons, Hugh continued to join Nell, their friends, and visitor Adrian Treleaven on coastal outings as Adrian worked on a book. Hugh later delivered the news to Lorna that Rufus Vane might recover, leading to her decision to take Rufus to Montreal for surgery. After returning from a Christmas spent in Brierley, Hugh later joined Nell, Lorna, Captain Saul, and Adrian by the hearth, where Captain Saul bestowed a blessing upon the gathered couples.

label: History
value: Cressida "Cressy" Lindsay is descended from an elite and established Bluenose lineage.
unit: Descended from an elite and established Bluenose lineage, Cressida "Cressy" Lindsay first met Nell and Honora at Old St. John's Cemetery while attending Wexcombe College, and the trio quickly established a warm friendship. Cressy used her social influence to aid her friends, and after enthusiastically begging to join them as a housemate, she moved into Tabby's Place for their remaining college years. During her time at Wexcombe, she frequently discussed her various potential suitors and potential marriage with her housemates. While staying at a boardinghouse in Prospect Point, Cressy developed feelings for a young theology student named Ezra Hale, eventually accepting his marriage proposal. She remained a close confidante to Nell throughout their studies, offering comfort and advice during Nell's various romantic troubles. After graduating and marrying Ezra, Cressy later gave birth to infants.

label: Quote
value: Cressy Lindsay said: "No, no, my dear. Shyness is not one of the numerous faults—or good qualities—possessed by Cressida Lindsay—Cressy as a nickname. Please use Cressy for me from the start. Well then, what are your names?"

label: Quote
value: Cressy Lindsay said: "Provided I am able to stroll alongside Honora and Wilfred, I will attend. Such an arrangement will render the chaperone role tolerable. Your Hugh is genuinely wonderful, Nell, yet what prompts his frequent company with Goggle-eyes?"

label: Quote
value: Cressy Lindsay said: "See—encircling the archway above the gate, written in white lettering. ‘Tabby’s Place.’ Isn’t that hilarious? Particularly along this Avenue filled with Pinehursts, Elmwolds, and Cedarcrofts? ‘Tabby’s Place,’ no less! I absolutely love it."

label: Quote
value: Cressy Lindsay said: "It’s true that they are exceptionally sweet boys, you know. An abundance of dances, drives, and overall festivities is planned. For failing to return home alongside me during the break, Queen Nell, you will never have my forgiveness."

label: Quote
value: Cressy Lindsay said: "I imagine a couple of quilting bees will take place; additionally, every old busybody will discuss you, both directly and in your absence. My dear, boredom will be the death of you."

value: Harcourt spent fourteen years living at Grey Shutters.

The following morning, friends and family gathered at the home to help prepare for the event. Hugh and Nell were subsequently married by Mr. Wace in the sunlit orchard, after which the newlyweds departed for Glen St. Agnes.

label: History
value: Honora Hollis attended Regent's Academy
unit: Honora Hollis attended Regent's Academy alongside Nell Harcourt and her classmates, where she spent a spring Saturday exploring the woods, named Crystal Lake, and listened to local stories. While employed at her home school, Honora later pursued further education, earning Honors in Classics at Wexcombe College. Upon arriving in Portmaris with Nell, Honora guided her to their boardinghouse and joined her in visiting Old St. John's Cemetery, where they befriended Cressida Lindsay. After deciding to lease a historic cottage called Tabby's Place for the school year, Honora and Nell successfully rented the home from Miss Tabby Linden and agreed to take in Cressy as a financial housemate. During her final year at Wexcombe, Honora continued living at Tabby's Place with her friends until graduation. She later married a foreign missionary.

label: History
value: During his school days, Hugh Carrow teased Nell Harcourt.
unit: During his school days, Hugh Carrow teased Nell Harcourt, prompting her to smash a slate over his head. Years later, he rescued her from a pond in his dory and offered his friendship, though she initially refused. After attending Regent's Academy and winning the Medal, Hugh selflessly withdrew his application for a teaching job in Brierley so Nell could take the position, leading the former rivals to reconcile. He later earned respect as Freshman Class president at Wexcombe College. Hugh eventually proposed to Nell, but she rejected his romantic advances to preserve their friendship, leaving him upset. After graduating with High Honors in Classics and the Cooper Prize, Hugh was stricken with a critical case of typhoid fever, but he survived the crisis. Following his recovery, he proposed again, and Nell happily accepted after they cleared up past misunderstandings. The two were married in a sunlit orchard and moved into a historic house in Seven Gulls Harbor, where Hugh pursued a medical career. Tragic heartbreak struck when their newborn daughter Joyce died shortly after birth, though they later welcomed a healthy baby boy named James Obed. Hugh also traveled to Montreal to facilitate a brain operation for a local man, which unmasked a long-held secret identity. Eventually, Hugh and Nell packed up their home and bade a tearful final farewell to Seven Gulls Harbor.

label: Quote
value: Hugh Carrow said: "People say it’s a pleasant old town, complete with the most splendid natural park anywhere. The landscape there is supposed to be grand, from what I’ve been told."

label: Quote
value: Hugh Carrow said: "Nell, you are merely fatigued. Come along, put everything out of your mind and go for a stroll with me—a trek back through the forest past the marsh. I ought to have something to display to you there."

label: Quote
value: Hugh Carrow said: "No. It is only because of a thing I witnessed over there during spring that I know it ought to be. Hurry. We will act as if we are a pair of youngsters once more, and we will travel whichever way the wind blows."

label: Quote
value: Isolde Duckett said: "My new home won't be distant. Our affection for one another will remain just as strong. That friendship ‘oath’ we pledged so many years ago has never been broken by us, has it?"

label: Quote
value: Isolde Duckett said: "Hold on until it is your turn, Miss Nell. Oh, Nell, my ear catches father walking up the stairs. Hand me my bouquet. Is my veil positioned correctly? Do I look extremely pale?"

label: Quote
value: Isolde Duckett said: "Naturally, there are ups and downs in married life. Expecting all things to proceed smoothly all the time is a mistake. However, Nell, I can give you my assurance that life is happy, provided your husband is the right man."

label: Quote
value: Isolde Duckett said: "Being so tall and slight, you will resemble a complete queen wearing it. Nell, in what manner DO you remain so thin? My weight has increased even more—before long, my waist will completely disappear."

label: Quote
value: Isolde Duckett said: "Oh, Nell—I am terribly anxious—I am unable to carry on—Nell, I am certain that I shall lose consciousness."

After her baby sister Posy Fay contracted croup, Isolde rushed to Grey Shutters for help, allowing Nell to nurse the infant until a doctor arrived. As they grew older, Isolde joined Nell in starting a private school story club and later helped bring the news of Nell's top placement on her entrance exams. Throughout their youth, Isolde actively participated in the Brierley Village Improvement Society alongside Nell, canvassing for donations and confronting Judson Tibbs over advertisement leases. Their adventures together included discovering Echo Cottage, searching for a rare willow-ware platter, and spending a rainy afternoon stranded near a duckhouse. Isolde eventually fell secretly in love with Gideon and happily confided her engagement to Nell. She maintained her close bond with Nell through her college years, offering feedback on Nell's early writing attempts and visiting Echo Cottage together. In a time of grief, Isolde joined Nell in walking home after the funeral of their friend Opal Pettigrew.

label: Quote
value: Isolde Pembroke said: "I am so happy that you have moved to Grey Shutters. Having a companion to play with will be wonderful. No other girls reside close enough for us to play together, and none of my sisters are old enough."

label: Quote
value: Isolde Pembroke said: "Nell, you are an unusual girl. I had previously been told that you were unusual. Even so, it seems to me that I am going to be very fond of you."

label: Quote
value: Isolde Pembroke said: “Yes,” Isolde replied, jerking her head back, “however, it is my belief that Julia Bell is not favored by him to such a high degree. I have listened to him state that he used her freckles to learn the multiplication table.”

label: Quote
value: Isolde Pembroke said: "Really, he teases every single girl. He makes jokes about mine on account of it being so black. He has named me a crow twelve times; and prior to this, I also have not known him to offer an apology for anything."

label: Quote
value: Isolde Pembroke said: "I really believe you are unkind. What am I to do? Mr. Pidgeon is going to force me to be seated next to that dreadful Tibby Tulk—I am certain he will since no one is sitting beside her. Please return, Nell."

label: History
value: Lorna Vane lost her brother when she was twelve.
unit: Lorna Vane's life was shaped by a history of hardship and grief, having lost her brother when she was twelve and finding her father's hanged body at age fourteen. She spent a year at Regent's Academy and eventually taught at the Glen school. Lorna formed a friendship with her neighbor Nell Harcourt, though she initially harbored feelings of envy and resentment toward Nell's happiness until she confessed her bitterness and the two became lifelong friends. When writer Adrian Treleaven stayed in the area, he was struck by Lorna's beauty, and she secretly fell in love with him before his cold departure left her heartbroken. Lorna later traveled to Montreal to secure surgery for the man she believed to be her husband, Rufus, only to discover that the man she had been married to for twelve years was actually his cousin, Laurence Vane. Upon returning home, Lorna was reunited with Adrian, who declared his love for her. As the couple planned their future together, Lorna shared that Adrian intended to buy Nell's former cottage to use for their summer holidays.

label: History
value: Lucy is a twin.
unit: As a newly orphaned twin, Lucy was brought alongside her brother Robin by Thirza Abernethy to live at Grey Shutters. Shortly after arriving, Robin enticed her outside, tricks her into jumping into a pigpen, and leaves her drenched under a water pump before walking into an Aid Society meeting. Later, Robin locked Lucy inside Mr. Pettifer's toolhouse, sparking a desperate search before she was found. After Nell returned to teaching, Lucy was terrified by Mirabel Cotton's stories of family ghosts, though her long-term future at Grey Shutters was secured when a trust fund was established following Richard Farrow's death. She later survived a monstrous hail storm that devastated the area, sheltering safely with her family at home. Eventually, Lucy was forced by Robin to skip Sunday School during a day of his rebellious behavior, though she continued to grow up at Grey Shutters, later attending family meals and gathering with loved ones to celebrate Nell's wedding in the orchard.

Later, Robin locked Lucy inside Mr. Pettifer's toolhouse, sparking a desperate search before she was found. After Nell returned to teaching, Lucy was terrified by Mirabel Cotton's stories of family ghosts, though her long-term future at Grey Shutters was secured when a trust fund was established following Richard Farrow's death. She later survived a monstrous hail storm that devastated the area, sheltering safely with her family at home. Eventually, Lucy was forced by Robin to skip Sunday School during a day of his rebellious behavior, though she continued to grow up at Grey Shutters, later attending family meals and gathering with loved ones to celebrate Nell's wedding in the orchard.

label: History
value: Mabel Colby attended Regent's Academy
unit: Mabel Colby attended Regent's Academy with Nell Harcourt and worked continuously as a schoolteacher after graduating, including a stint in an isolated rural school. Facing limited financial means, Mabel sent a letter to Nell proposing that Nell, Honora, and Mabel lease a house together for the upcoming school year. The women successfully moved into Tabby's Place in Portmaris alongside other housemates to share living expenses. While living together, Mabel complained about rising prices during an evening study session. During her final year at Wexcombe, Mabel combated study fatigue on a rainy night by reviewing old Story Club tales with Nell.

value: Mabel Colby said: "Cressy, you make no sense to me. It is obvious you are intentionally encouraging him, yet you are fully aware that your intentions are not serious."

label: Quote
value: Mabel Colby said: "My fear was that they would return, which would shatter our delightful small haven here, casting us unfortunate, inexperienced young ones back into the harsh realm of boardinghouses."

label: Quote
value: Mabel Colby said: "Oh, Nell, my intellect concurs with what you say. Nevertheless, my spirit continues to be gloomy and lacking in creative spark. Rainy evenings perpetually leave me feeling filthy and unkempt."

label: Quote

label: Appearance
value: Nell has a slight, slender frame.
unit: Nell possesses a slight, slender frame with a straight-backed figure, standing an inch taller than Isolde Pembroke. Her features include a bright, ethereal face with a sharp, small pointed chin, a pleasant and pretty nose dusted with seven freckles, and a slender, alabaster neck. She has large, starry gray eyes, which have also been noted as gleaming gray-green, set against a freckled, milk-white complexion with cheeks that easily show a rose hue. Her hair is prominently described as red, ginger, fiery, or auburn, often worn in long crimson braids or plaits, though it has also appeared green at times.

value: Obed Abernethy is quiet.
unit: Obed Abernethy is a quiet, reserved, and extremely shy individual who tends to be silent, bashful, and uncommunicative in social settings. He is exceptionally timid, holding a deep-seated fear of women—with the exception of Thirza and Mrs. Agatha—as well as little girls. He despises being surrounded by unfamiliar people or visiting places where he might be expected to converse, often preferring to retreat into the shadows. Despite his taciturn nature, he is a gentle, patient, and good-natured listener who appreciates talkative companions. However, he is also remarkably stubborn, possessing a habit of adopting a caprice and tenaciously clinging to his view regardless of logic or reasoning.

label: History
value: Obed Abernethy was a quiet man.
unit: Obed Abernethy was a quiet, timid man who wore a thick brown beard and lived at Grey Shutters with his sister, Thirza. Driven by a desire for help on their farm, he set out to pick up a Nova Scotian orphan boy, only to discover an orphan girl named Nell waiting for him instead. Taking her into his buggy, he enjoyed her chatty company and brought her home. Although Thirza initially intended to send Nell back to the asylum, Obed quietly wished to keep her and later persuaded Nell to apologize to a neighbor after a outburst, smoothing over her stay. Over the years, he offered the young girl gentle affection and consistent support. Noticing her poor wardrobe, he enlisted help to buy fabric and have a stylish gown made for her as a Christmas surprise. When Nell took her entrance exams, Obed joined the family in proudly celebrating her top results. He also gave her his steady encouragement as she pursued her education, right up until her graduation. Tragically, upon learning that their savings bank had failed, Obed suffered a collapse and died, leaving Thirza and Nell to mourn his loss at Grey Shutters.

label: Personality
value: Odette Pullen is unassuming.
unit: Odette Pullen is an unassuming, hardworking, and dutiful individual who earns top marks in domestic science and possesses great culinary skills. Characterized by a steady, sensible, and pragmatic nature, she maintains a notable composure that makes her appear completely unshakeable. She is regarded as lady-like, pleasant, and unpretentious, maintaining a gentle disposition and a tranquil, rosy-faced nature that remains unsoured despite marital arguments. Though she finds teaching tedious, she initially intends to dedicate her life to pedagogy and forgo marriage forever. She later surrenders her position at the Brierley school with plans to travel West during the autumn.

label: History
value: Before starting her teaching career, Odette Pullen secured a school teaching position in Stonebridge.
unit: Before starting her teaching career, Odette Pullen secured a school teaching position in Stonebridge, having previously spent four weeks tearfully reacting to the departure of the former schoolmaster, Mr. Pidgeon. During a romantic theatrical play of Elaine, she was cast as Guinevere, and on a separate occasion, her brother saved her sash just as she nearly tumbled into the Lake of Glassy Waters while reaching for water lilies. Later, Odette arrived with her brother Barney to escort friends to a charity concert at the Pale Sands Hotel, where they shared supper and enjoyed the evening together. Before beginning her upcoming teaching term, she joined Nell Harcourt and Hugh Carrow to discuss their differing views on classroom discipline. On a spring Saturday, Odette spent the day exploring Crystal Lake and an abandoned garden alongside Nell, Honora, and Isolde. As a member of a local delegation from the Village Improvement Society, she accompanied Nell and Isolde to confront Judson Tibbs over his plans for commercial advertising on his fence. Later, on New Year's Eve, Odette proposed marriage to Nell on behalf of her bashful brother Barney, but reacted with cool indifference when Nell rejected the offer. Her successful work in Stonebridge earned her a place on the Inspector's Roll of Honor before she eventually made plans to move West. She later visited Grey Shutters to offer her well-wishes to Nell ahead of Nell's upcoming wedding to Hugh Carrow.

label: Quote

label: Quote

label: Quote

label: Personality
value: Opal Pettigrew possesses a sunny, pleasant disposition.
unit: Opal Pettigrew possesses a sunny, pleasant disposition, delights openly in the enjoyable aspects of life, and is prone to laughter, though she also tends toward sentimentality and hysteria. Her thoughts and motivations are heavily consumed by romantic pursuits, including plans to secure a boyfriend at age fifteen, teach briefly after qualifying, and entertain dozens of suitors to drive them wild before eventually settling down. Despite her lighthearted focus on male attention and suitors, she harbors intense fears of plump green caterpillars, lying flat and pretending to be deceased on a floating craft, and the unfamiliarity of the afterlife.

label: History
value: Opal Pettigrew grew up with numerous older sisters.
unit: Opal Pettigrew grew up with numerous older sisters who were quickly married off, having expressed a childhood ambition to possess dozens of suitors. In her youth, she had her warts cured using an enchanted stone from old Mary Joe, and she once hid in a hallway pantry when her sister Tabitha received a marriage proposal from Malcolm Andres. She attended school and Regent's alongside Nell Harcourt, and during a past autumn she visited Boston. After Nelson Atkins proposed to her, she returned home and composed a blistering rejection letter. During a break from college, Nell learned from Mrs. Sowerby that Opal was gravely ill with consumption. Nell visited Opal, who tearfully confessed her fear of dying and her unfulfilled desires for her life before passing away peacefully in her sleep shortly thereafter.

label: History
value: Mr. Pettifer is a lifelong bachelor
unit: A lifelong bachelor who had delayed marriage for too long, Mr. Pettifer originally lived in Scottsford, New Brunswick, before relocating to Brierley. Having routinely been flogged by his schoolmaster as a boy, he kept a pet parrot named Nutmeg, which had been given to him by his brother, a sailor. His relationship with his neighbor Nell got off to a tense start when he angrily confronted her over a cow escaping into his oat field; however, after Nell mistakenly sold his Jersey cow and offered a trade, he took the mistake generously and invited her for tea. He later turned down Nell's request for a community donation, but he continued to engage in friendly local debates with her. During a severe hailstorm, lightning struck his home and killed Nutmeg, though he was comforted by Nell and eventually reconciled with his wife, Emily, sharing the story of their marriage and quarrel over the parrot. Pettifer also encouraged Nell's literary pursuits, offering critiques on a manuscript she wrote and advising her to keep writing about what she knew after her initial rejections. He later visited Nell at Grey Shutters during a severe winter snowstorm to deliver her mail, which contained news of an inheritance.

label: History
value: Robin Farrow was brought to live at Grey Shutters.
unit: Robin Farrow, a former troublemaker, was brought to live at Grey Shutters with his twin sister, Lucy, by Thirza Abernethy after becoming an orphan. Early on, he proved prone to mischief, such as tricking Lucy into a pigpen and getting her wet under a water pump. He later locked Lucy in Mr. Pettifer's toolhouse and broke down in tears when confronted, admitting he did not realize lying was wrong, which earned him a punishment of going to bed without dinner. His antics continued as he accidentally ruined lemon pies intended for guests and knocked over a shell that shattered a borrowed platter. Despite his antics, he bonded closely with Nell, seeking her comfort when he felt jealous of others or worried about her affections. Following the death of Richard Farrow, a trust fund was established for Robin and Lucy, allowing them to permanently reside at Grey Shutters. During a severe storm, Robin sheltered at home with the family as hail devastated the area. When Nell left for college, a distressed Robin questioned her departure, though he later sent her letters filled with local news and descriptions of his ongoing mischief. While Nell was away, Robin rebelled against Mrs. Sowerby's strict rules by throwing away collection money, forcing Lucy to skip Sunday School, and telling lies, but he eventually confessed his guilt to Nell. As time passed, he matured and attended Nell's orchard wedding to Hugh Carrow, later receiving an invitation from Captain Saul to visit him at the lighthouse during a festive Christmas gathering.

He later locked Lucy in Mr. Pettifer's toolhouse and broke down in tears when confronted, admitting he did not realize lying was wrong, which earned him a punishment of going to bed without dinner. His antics continued as he accidentally ruined lemon pies intended for guests and knocked over a shell that shattered a borrowed platter. Despite his antics, he bonded closely with Nell, seeking her comfort when he felt jealous of others or worried about her affections. Following the death of Richard Farrow, a trust fund was established for Robin and Lucy, allowing them to permanently reside at Grey Shutters. During a severe storm, Robin sheltered at home with the family as hail devastated the area. When Nell left for college, a distressed Robin questioned her departure, though he later sent her letters filled with local news and descriptions of his ongoing mischief. While Nell was away, Robin rebelled against Mrs. Sowerby's strict rules by throwing away collection money, forcing Lucy to skip Sunday School, and telling lies, but he eventually confessed his guilt to Nell. As time passed, he matured and attended Nell's orchard wedding to Hugh Carrow, later receiving an invitation from Captain Saul to visit him at the lighthouse during a festive Christmas gathering.

label: Quote
value: Robin Farrow said: "You do not seem like the kind of lady who would lash a small boy simply because he was unable to stay motionless. Did you not find staying motionless terribly difficult when you were merely as old as I am?"

label: Quote
value: Robin Farrow said: "Thirza did the laundry yesterday . . . and Mrs. Wiggins scrubbed my skin using hard soap on the funeral day. For a single week, that suffices. Being so exceedingly clean seems pointless to me. Staying dirty is far more comfortable."

label: Quote
value: Robin Farrow said: "However, the caterpillar was so amazingly large . . . I grabbed him from the church steps right as we entered. Wasting him appeared to be a shame. Also, tell me, was it not amusing listening to that girl scream?"

label: Quote
value: Robin Farrow said: "I only carried it out for amusement. Events have been extraordinarily quiet in this place for such a long time that I believed scaring you people immensely would prove entertaining. Indeed, it turned out to be so."

label: Quote
value: Robin Farrow said: “Why?” asked Robin, making himself comfortable and gazing upward with a tear-streaked, probing countenance. “Why is whopper not as good as falsehood? I want to know. It is an equally large word.”

value: Rufus Vane inherited a nautical inclination from his mother.

While in Cuba, Rufus contracted yellow fever and passed away thirteen years ago, forcing his vessel, the Four Sisters, to leave without him. For twelve years following his death, his cousin Laurence Vane masqueraded in his place before the truth of Rufus's passing was ultimately revealed.

label: History
value: Tabitha never married.
unit: Tabitha never married and was never courted or proposed to by any man, though she held no ill feelings toward men and would have gladly wed had the opportunity arisen. She stepped in to assist Nell and Hugh by taking over the household chores so that Nell could rest. Later, Tabitha arrived with news that her sister had broken her leg, which prompted Lorna to temporarily move in with Nell and Hugh. After Lorna and Adrian declared their love for each other, Tabitha returned to the house bringing local gossip.

label: Quote
value: Tabitha said: "Enjoy yourself and refrain from stressing over the kitchen supplies. The steering is in Tabitha’s hands. Owning a dog is pointless if you bark yourself. Each morning, I will bring breakfast up to your room."

label: Quote
value: Tabitha said: "That he remains unmarried is truly strange, because a person of his sort could win anyone just by asking. Well, perhaps he resembles me and has hitherto failed to encounter his proper match."

label: Quote
value: Tabitha said: "Should you be unable to, I shall refrain from attending, Mrs. Doctor, dear, despite Matilda’s leg. I refuse to cause you anxiety, and to have that sweet child disturbed as a result, for all the legs in existence."

label: Quote
value: Tabitha said: "It is my belief that some food and drink will be welcomed by us all. Instruct young Mrs. Doctor to be entirely free of concern—Tabitha is taking charge. Instruct her to occupy her thoughts solely with her infant."

label: Quote
value: Tabitha said: "Never before have I beheld a newborn so pale—normally they are reddish or yellowish. Furthermore, its large eyes unclosed just like a baby several months along. That tiny, tiny creature! Oh, that tragic, youthful Mrs. Doctor!"

value: Thirza has a tall frame.

Though she once anticipated becoming completely blind, her failing eyesight has significantly improved and stabilized, remaining at a state where it is unlikely to fail further or improve dramatically.

label: History
value: Thirza Abernethy lived at Grey Shutters for sixty years after reaching adulthood.
unit: Thirza Abernethy lived at Grey Shutters for sixty years after reaching adulthood, having previously wallpapered a spare bedroom with her brother Obed's help. When Obed brought an orphan girl named Nell to Grey Shutters by mistake instead of a boy, Thirza initially insisted the child be returned to the asylum, but she soon agreed to keep her. She provided religious guidance to Nell and raised her through various childhood misadventures, including cutting Nell's hair short after a disastrous dyeing incident. Thirza later supported Nell's academic ambitions, celebrating her top entrance exam results and offering comfort when Obed died following a sudden bank failure. To help manage her failing eyesight and keep Grey Shutters, Thirza agreed to have Agatha Sowerby move in while Nell attended college. Over the years, she also took in two orphaned twins, Robin and Lucy Farrow, raising them permanently after their father's trust fund was established. Thirza watched Nell mature, eventually helping prepare for Nell's wedding to Hugh Carrow in the Grey Shutters orchard. She later traveled to Seven Gulls Harbor—her first journey of sixty miles from home—to visit the couple for Christmas and assist Nell through pregnancy and childbirth.

value: Thora lived at Wayside in Coombe Road.
unit: Thora lived at Wayside in Coombe Road, where she hosted Nell Harcourt as a lodger and was courted by her long-term suitor, John Fairlie. After twenty years of courting without a proposal, Thora broke down to Nell and subsequently rejected John coldly following a prayer meeting. However, after John's mother passed away, John explained that his late mother had forced him into a secret vow not to marry while she was alive; he then proposed, and Thora agreed to marry him.

label: History
value: Captain Saul welcomes Nell and Hugh to their new home.
unit: Captain Saul, also known as Uncle Saul, welcomes Nell and Hugh to their new home and becomes a frequent presence in their lives, sharing stories of local history and his time at sea. Operating the Seven Gulls Point lighthouse, he hosts gatherings where he introduces neighbors and entertains visitors with his collection of sea curiosities. He attends Christmas dinner with Nell, Hugh, and other friends, engaging in lively debate, and welcomes the New Year at the lighthouse surrounded by companions. Later, Saul comforts Nell during her grief over the loss of her newborn daughter, Joyce, and entrusts her with the story of his own long-lost love, Margaret. When Adrian Treleaven visits Seven Gulls Point, Saul realizes Adrian is the grandson of Damaris Tremayne, lends him his personal life log, and agrees to let Adrian write a book based on his seafaring adventures and his lost Margaret. Saul later provides funds to Lorna Vane so she can travel to Montreal for surgery on her supposed brother Rufus. Following a Liberal political victory, he contemplates his own mortality, asking Nell to care for his cat, First Mate, after he passes away. After bestowing a heartfelt blessing on Adrian and Lorna upon their engagement, Saul receives the printed copy of his life story, celebrating its arrival with Nell and Lorna. unit: Captain Saul, also known as Uncle Saul, welcomes Nell and Hugh to their new home and becomes a frequent presence in their lives, sharing stories of local history and his time at sea. Operating the Seven Gulls Point lighthouse, he hosts gatherings where he introduces neighbors and entertains visitors with his collection of sea curiosities. He attends Christmas dinner with Nell, Hugh, and other friends, engaging in lively debate, and welcomes the New Year at the lighthouse surrounded by companions. Later, Saul comforts Nell during her grief over the loss of her newborn daughter, Joyce, and entrusts her with the story of his own long-lost love, Margaret. When Adrian Treleaven visits Seven Gulls Point, Saul realizes Adrian is the grandson of Damaris Tremayne, lends him his personal life log, and agrees to let Adrian write a book based on his seafaring adventures and his lost Margaret. Saul later provides funds to Lorna Vane so she can travel to Montreal for surgery on her supposed brother Rufus. Following a Liberal political victory, he contemplates his own mortality, asking Nell to care for his cat, First Mate, after he passes away. After bestowing a heartfelt blessing on Adrian and Lorna upon their engagement, Saul receives the printed copy of his life story, celebrating its arrival with Nell and Lorna. The following morning, Hugh and Nell discover that Captain Saul has peacefully passed away at the lighthouse with his book open on his chest.

label: Quote
value: Uncle Saul said: "Nephew Hector. His understanding of it matches my own. Well, now, I am truly pleased that you invited me to remain for supper. My hunger is quite strong—I ate very little for dinner today."

label: Quote
value: Uncle Saul said: "Listen, my usual way of living is royal. Up at the Glen yesterday evening, two pounds of steak were bought by me to bring back. Today, my intention was to enjoy an extraordinarily fine dinner."

label: Quote
value: Uncle Saul said: "Indeed, I fear that is the case. I really dislike it. It gives me the impression that there might be something rather unnatural concerning myself."

label: Quote
value: Uncle Saul said: “Probably—probably,” agreed Captain Saul. “That’s what I remarked to him back then. Thinking that was a great deal more reassuring. I disliked the thought of him perceiving stuff of that nature—it felt truly strange.”

label: Quote
value: Uncle Saul said: "Those were the words he used. I recall them just as if it happened yesterday, even if I was not entirely sure what he intended to say. What is your guess about what he REALLY intended, doctor?"

label: History
value: Wilfred Mott defended Nell Harcourt's honor.
unit: In his youth, Wilfred Mott defended Nell Harcourt's honor by getting into a fight with Elias Purdy MacKinnon after Elias criticized Nell's recitations, and he previously declared to his mother that Nell was the cleverest female student in school. Having written local newspaper pieces in the past, he was infatuated with Nell when she was seventeen. Years later, Wilfred traveled by train and ferry alongside Nell and Hugh Carrow as they journeyed to Portmaris. While attending college, he joined Nell, Hugh, Honora Hollis, and Cressida Lindsay on a walk along Linden Avenue. During Nell's term at Wexcombe, Wilfred made an unpleasant proposal to her, which she did not accept.

label: History
value: Miss Winifred Tolley spent eight years as an only child.
unit: Miss Winifred Tolley spent eight years as an only child, missing having siblings, until her younger brother was born. After her mother passed away before her brother reached his third birthday, she served as both a sister and a mother to him. In her earlier life, she helped construct a church at Glen St. Agnes alongside other women and won an award for lemon pies at the Port Marlow Exhibition. Later living in Seven Gulls, Miss Winifred frequently visited Nell and Hugh Harcourt, sharing her sharp, opinionated views on neighbors, local gossip, ministers, and local history. During these visits, she shared the tragic background of Lorna Vane's family and later brought news that journalist Adrian Treleaven would be staying in the village. After a medical trip to Montreal revealed that Lorna's husband was actually his cousin Laurence Vane, Miss Winifred discussed the revelation with Nell and suggested that Nell notify Adrian of Lorna's freedom. Later, Miss Winifred approved of Lorna staying with Nell during Adrian's visit, and she subsequently announced her own upcoming marriage to Ambrose Kerr.

value: Winifred Tolley said: "She has altered considerably of late. Her laughter and jesting resemble those of a young girl, and based on what she says, I deduce she visits this place quite frequently."

label: Quote
value: Winifred Tolley said: "MR. Fiske, my lone brother passed away fifteen years back, and I’ve taken on no new ones since then. Regarding my Christian faith, I trust and believe I possessed it while you were still a toddler wearing petticoats."

label: Quote
value: Winifred Tolley said: "Nell, are you trying to say that the rumors I’ve been hearing are factual—that Dr. Carrow informed Lorna that Rufus can be healed, and that she intends to bring him to Montreal so he can undergo surgery?"

label: Quote
value: Winifred Tolley said: "Rufus Vane received the harm that resulted in his current state during a drunken brawl. His fate is DESERVED. It was inflicted upon him as a retribution. The doctor, I don’t believe, has any right to meddle with God’s visitations."

label: Quote
value: Winifred Tolley said: "Now, you don't need to call me Miss Winifred, my dear Nell. EVERYONE would have come to the identical conclusion. Should the physicians in Montreal succeed in transforming Rufus Vane into a sensible person, they are truly remarkable."

label: v1 · CHAPTER XV. A Tempest in the School Teapot
value: Hugh Carrow teases Nell about her red hair.
chapter: v1 · CHAPTER XV. A Tempest in the School Teapot
unit: In class, Hugh Carrow teases Nell about her red hair, prompting her to smash her slate over his head in anger. Mr. Pidgeon punishes Nell by forcing her to stand at the front of the room and later making her sit beside Hugh, leading Nell to declare that she will never return to school. Upon returning home, Thirza Abernethy seeks advice from Agatha Sowerby, who recommends letting Nell rest at home until her temper subsides.

chapter: v2 · II Selling in Haste and Repenting at Leisure
unit: On their way back from shopping in Delford, Nell and Isolde chase a Jersey cow out of a neighbor's oat field, and Nell impulsively sells the cow to Mr. Shearer. Upon returning home to Grey Shutters, Nell discovers her own cow is still in the pen, realizing she mistakenly sold Mr. Pettifer's cow instead. Resigned to face his temper, Nell packs a freshly baked nut cake as a peace offering and sets off to confess her mistake to Mr. Pettifer.

value: Nell and Isolde chase a Jersey cow out of a neighbor's oat field.
chapter: v2 · II Selling in Haste and Repenting at Leisure
unit: On their way back from shopping in Delford, Nell and Isolde chase a Jersey cow out of a neighbor's oat field, and Nell impulsively sells the cow to Mr. Shearer. Upon returning home to Grey Shutters, Nell discovers her own cow is still in the pen, realizing she mistakenly sold Mr. Pettifer's cow instead. Resigned to face his temper, Nell packs a freshly baked nut cake as a peace offering and sets off to confess her mistake to Mr. Pettifer.

label: v2 · V A Full-fledged Schoolma’am
value: Nell begins her first day teaching school in Brierley.
chapter: v2 · V A Full-fledged Schoolma’am
unit: Nell begins her first day teaching school in Brierley, observing the various pupils in her classroom and forming an immediate warm connection with Cedric Stanhope. After dealing with minor disciplinary issues and feeling exhausted by the day's end, she is visited by an overly eccentric mother, Mrs. Trask, who insists on specific pronunciations and names for her children. Afterwards, Cedric gifts Nell wild orchids on her walk home, lifting her spirits before she reflects on the day with Thirza and Agatha Sowerby.

unit: Nell dismisses school early as a monstrous storm approaches, exactly as Uncle Zeb predicted. unit: Thirza brings the newly orphaned twins, Robin and Lucy, back to live at Grey Shutters. unit: At a party hosted by Isolde Pembroke, Nell Harcourt accepts a dare from Flossie Tulk to walk across the kitchen roof's ridgepole. She slips and falls, breaking her ankle in the process. chapter: v1 · CHAPTER XXXI. Where the Brook and River Meet
unit: Nell enjoys a relaxing, healthy summer after a doctor advises outdoor play to preserve her health. Returning to her studies in autumn, she works hard under Miss Thorne's guidance to prepare for the upcoming Entrance examination despite her growing anxieties. As she physically matures and reflects on her changes, Thirza experiences a bittersweet realization of Nell growing up.

label: v1 · CHAPTER XXXII. The Pass List Is Out
value: Nell completes her entrance examinations in town.
chapter: v1 · CHAPTER XXXII. The Pass List Is Out
unit: Nell completes her entrance examinations in town, staying with Aunt Lavinia, and returns to Brierley to anxiously await the results. After weeks of tense waiting, Isolde brings the newspaper showing that Nell tied for first place on the island. Overjoyed, Nell shares the glorious news with Obed, Thirza, and Mrs. Sowerby.

value: Thirza returns from the eye doctor.
chapter: v1 · CHAPTER XXXVIII. The Bend in the Road
unit: Thirza returns from the eye doctor with bad news that her vision is severely failing and she must avoid eye strain, prompting her to consider selling Grey Shutters. Nell insists on giving up her college scholarship to stay home, care for Thirza, and teach locally so they can keep their home. Later, Mrs. Sowerby reveals that Hugh Carrow selflessly withdrew his application for the Brierley school so Nell could teach there, and Nell thanks Hugh when she runs into him.

Isolde Pembroke rushes in to ask for help when her baby sister, Posy Fay, contracts croup while their parents are away. Nell uses her experience to treat Posy Fay through the night until a doctor arrives, saving the child's life before returning home to rest.

chapter: v1 · CHAPTER XXIII. Nell Comes to Grief in an Affair of Honor
unit: At a party hosted by Isolde Pembroke, Nell Harcourt accepts a dare from Flossie Tulk to walk across the kitchen roof's ridgepole. She slips and falls, breaking her ankle in the process. Mr. Pembroke carries her home to Thirza Abernethy, and Nell spends the next seven weeks recovering in bed while friends, neighbors, and local figures visit her.

label: v1 · CHAPTER XXVI. The Story Club Is Formed
value: Routine resumes at Brierley.
chapter: v1 · CHAPTER XXVI. The Story Club Is Formed
unit: Following the excitement of the school concert, routine resumes at Brierley while Nell and Isolde discuss turning thirteen and working on school essays along the Aspen Path. chapter: v2 · II Selling in Haste and Repenting at Leisure
unit: On their way back from shopping in Delford, Nell and Isolde chase a Jersey cow out of a neighbor's oat field, and Nell impulsively sells the cow to Mr. Shearer. Upon returning home to Grey Shutters, Nell discovers her own cow is still in the pen, realizing she mistakenly sold Mr. Pettifer's cow instead. Resigned to face his temper, Nell packs a freshly baked nut cake as a peace offering and sets off to confess her mistake to Mr. Pettifer.

chapter: v1 · CHAPTER XVIII. Nell to the Rescue
unit: While Thirza and Mrs. Sowerby attend a political rally in town, Nell and Obed spend a quiet evening at Grey Shutters. Isolde Pembroke rushes in to ask for help when her baby sister, Posy Fay, contracts croup while their parents are away. Nell uses her experience to treat Posy Fay through the night until a doctor arrives, saving the child's life before returning home to rest.

unit: At a party hosted by Isolde Pembroke, Nell Harcourt accepts a dare from Flossie Tulk to walk across the kitchen roof's ridgepole. She slips and falls, breaking her ankle in the process. unit: Nell wakes up at Grey Shutters and marvels at the bright June morning outside her window, though she laments that her stay will likely be brief. unit: While Thirza and Mrs. Sowerby attend a political rally in town, Nell and Obed spend a quiet evening at Grey Shutters. Isolde Pembroke rushes in to ask for help when her baby sister, Posy Fay, contracts croup while their parents are away. Nell uses her experience to treat Posy Fay through the night until a doctor arrives, saving the child's life before returning home to rest.

unit: While Thirza and Mrs. Sowerby attend a political rally in town, Nell and Obed spend a quiet evening at Grey Shutters. unit: Nell walks home through the woods, chatting with Isolde Pembroke along the way. Upon arriving at Grey Shutters, she learns from Thirza Abernethy that young Lucy has gone missing, sparking a desperate search that eventually leads to finding Lucy locked in Mr. Pettifer's toolhouse by Robin Farrow. When confronted about his trickery and lying, Robin breaks down in tears, admitting he didn't realize lying was wrong, leading Nell and Thirza to forgive the lies while determining how to discipline him for locking Lucy away.

value: Nell walks home through the woods.

unit: Nell walks home through the woods, chatting with Isolde Pembroke along the way. Upon arriving at Grey Shutters, she learns from Thirza Abernethy that young Lucy has gone missing, sparking a desperate search that eventually leads to finding Lucy locked in Mr. Pettifer's toolhouse by Robin Farrow. When confronted about his trickery and lying, Robin breaks down in tears, admitting he didn't realize lying was wrong, leading Nell and Thirza to forgive the lies while determining how to discipline him for locking Lucy away.

unit: In class, Hugh Carrow teases Nell about her red hair, prompting her to smash her slate over his head in anger. Mr. Pidgeon punishes Nell by forcing her to stand at the front of the room and later making her sit beside Hugh, leading Nell to declare that she will never return to school. Upon returning home, Thirza Abernethy seeks advice from Agatha Sowerby, who recommends letting Nell rest at home until her temper subsides.

unit: While Thirza and Mrs. Sowerby attend a political rally in town, Nell and Obed spend a quiet evening at Grey Shutters. Nell uses her experience to treat Posy Fay through the night until a doctor arrives, saving the child's life before returning home to rest.

label: v1 · CHAPTER IV. Morning at Grey Shutters
value: Nell wakes up at Grey Shutters.
chapter: v1 · CHAPTER IV. Morning at Grey Shutters
unit: Nell wakes up at Grey Shutters and marvels at the bright June morning outside her window, though she laments that her stay will likely be brief. During breakfast and while helping with household chores, she talks incessantly to a sharp yet increasingly fascinated Thirza, even bestowing names like Frost Maiden on the cherry tree and Bonny on the geranium. Afterwards, Thirza takes Nell in the buggy to Pale Sands to meet Mrs. Tranter and settle Nell's return to Nova Scotia, despite Obed's quiet desire to keep the girl.

When Thirza asks her to fetch an apron pattern from the Pembrokes, Nell confesses that she and Isolde invented ghosts in the nearby wood, making her terrified to cross it in the dark. Unmoved, Thirza forces Nell to walk through the woods to teach her a lesson, and Nell reluctantly completes the frightening errand.

unit: At a party hosted by Isolde Pembroke, Nell Harcourt accepts a dare from Flossie Tulk to walk across the kitchen roof's ridgepole. She slips and falls, breaking her ankle in the process. Mr. Pembroke carries her home to Thirza Abernethy, and Nell spends the next seven weeks recovering in bed while friends, neighbors, and local figures visit her.

value: Nell and Isolde chase a Jersey cow out of a neighbor's oat field.
chapter: v2 · II Selling in Haste and Repenting at Leisure
unit: On their way back from shopping in Delford, Nell and Isolde chase a Jersey cow out of a neighbor's oat field, and Nell impulsively sells the cow to Mr. Shearer. Upon returning home to Grey Shutters, Nell discovers her own cow is still in the pen, realizing she mistakenly sold Mr. Pettifer's cow instead. Resigned to face his temper, Nell packs a freshly baked nut cake as a peace offering and sets off to confess her mistake to Mr. Pettifer.

unit: Nell walks home through the woods, chatting with Isolde Pembroke along the way. Upon arriving at Grey Shutters, she learns from Thirza Abernethy that young Lucy has gone missing, sparking a desperate search that eventually leads to finding Lucy locked in Mr. Pettifer's toolhouse by Robin Farrow. When confronted about his trickery and lying, Robin breaks down in tears, admitting he didn't realize lying was wrong, leading Nell and Thirza to forgive the lies while determining how to discipline him for locking Lucy away.

value: Nell walks home through the woods.
chapter: v2 · X Robin in Search of a Sensation
unit: Nell walks home through the woods, chatting with Isolde Pembroke along the way. Upon arriving at Grey Shutters, she learns from Thirza Abernethy that young Lucy has gone missing, sparking a desperate search that eventually leads to finding Lucy locked in Mr. Pettifer's toolhouse by Robin Farrow. When confronted about his trickery and lying, Robin breaks down in tears, admitting he didn't realize lying was wrong, leading Nell and Thirza to forgive the lies while determining how to discipline him for locking Lucy away.

Upon returning home, Thirza Abernethy seeks advice from Agatha Sowerby, who recommends letting Nell rest at home until her temper subsides.

unit: Nell walks home through the woods, chatting with Isolde Pembroke along the way. When confronted about his trickery and lying, Robin breaks down in tears, admitting he didn't realize lying was wrong, leading Nell and Thirza to forgive the lies while determining how to discipline him for locking Lucy away.

chapter: v1 · CHAPTER IV. Morning at Grey Shutters
unit: Nell wakes up at Grey Shutters and marvels at the bright June morning outside her window, though she laments that her stay will likely be brief. During breakfast and while helping with household chores, she talks incessantly to a sharp yet increasingly fascinated Thirza, even bestowing names like Frost Maiden on the cherry tree and Bonny on the geranium. Afterwards, Thirza takes Nell in the buggy to Pale Sands to meet Mrs. Tranter and settle Nell's return to Nova Scotia, despite Obed's quiet desire to keep the girl.

value: Nell wakes up at Grey Shutters.
chapter: CHAPTER IV. Morning at Grey Shutters
unit: Nell wakes up at Grey Shutters and marvels at the bright June morning outside her window, though she laments that her stay will likely be brief. During breakfast and while helping with household chores, she talks incessantly to a sharp yet increasingly fascinated Thirza, even bestowing names like Frost Maiden on the cherry tree and Bonny on the geranium. Afterwards, Thirza takes Nell in the buggy to Pale Sands to meet Mrs. Tranter and settle Nell's return to Nova Scotia, despite Obed's quiet desire to keep the girl.

chapter: CHAPTER XI. Nell’s Impressions of Sunday-school

unit: In her room at Grey Shutters, Nell reflects on her first year with Thirza, who admits she does not regret keeping her. When Thirza asks her to fetch an apron pattern from the Pembrokes, Nell confesses that she and Isolde invented ghosts in the nearby wood, making her terrified to cross it in the dark. Unmoved, Thirza forces Nell to walk through the woods to teach her a lesson, and Nell reluctantly completes the frightening errand.

value: Nell and Isolde are on their way back from shopping in Delford.
chapter: II Selling in Haste and Repenting at Leisure
unit: On their way back from shopping in Delford, Nell and Isolde chase a Jersey cow out of a neighbor's oat field, and Nell impulsively sells the cow to Mr. Shearer. Upon returning home to Grey Shutters, Nell discovers her own cow is still in the pen, realizing she mistakenly sold Mr. Pettifer's cow instead. Resigned to face his temper, Nell packs a freshly baked nut cake as a peace offering and sets off to confess her mistake to Mr. Pettifer.

chapter: V A Full-fledged Schoolma’am
unit: Nell begins her first day teaching school in Brierley, observing the various pupils in her classroom and forming an immediate warm connection with Cedric Stanhope. After dealing with minor disciplinary issues and feeling exhausted by the day's end, she is visited by an overly eccentric mother, Mrs. Trask, who insists on specific pronunciations and names for her children. Afterwards, Cedric gifts Nell wild orchids on her walk home, lifting her spirits before she reflects on the day with Thirza and Agatha Sowerby.

label: XVII A Chapter of Accidents
value: Nell spends the morning preparing Grey Shutters.
chapter: XVII A Chapter of Accidents
unit: Nell and Isolde spend the morning busily preparing Grey Shutters and cooking a lavish meal to welcome Mrs. Varley, but Robin accidentally ruins the lemon pies and gets sent to his room. When Mrs. Varley and Honora fail to arrive, the group sits down to eat without them, only to discover the peas have been over-sweetened by multiple cooks. To make matters worse, as dinner ends, Robin accidentally knocks a heavy shell down the stairs, shattering Miss Pembroke's borrowed platter.

unit: Nell writes a story titled 'Evadne's Atonement', sharing her process and drafts with Isolde and seeking feedback from Mr. Pettifer. unit: Nell, Hugh, and Lorna walk to Seven Gulls Point lighthouse on New Year's Eve, catching a rare glimpse of Venus's shadow along the way. As midnight strikes, Captain Saul opens the door to welcome the New Year and offers a hopeful toast to all present.

Meanwhile, Captain Saul shares his written life log with Nell, who wishes a talented writer like Cedric could turn his adventurous life into a book.

chapter: CHAPTER 39 CAPTAIN SAUL CROSSES THE BAR
unit: Nell and Lorna deliver Adrian Treleaven and James Garrick's finished book to Captain Saul, who celebrates its arrival with tea and cake. The next morning, Hugh notices that the lighthouse light is still burning past sunrise. Hugh and Nell hasten to the lighthouse, where they find Captain Saul has peacefully passed away with his life-book open on his chest.
